To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capital market has systemic problems that are not being addressed by the IMF and that the IMF should be transformed into a global central bank.

(1) the global nature of capital flows and the volatility of these flows are the result of a combination of systemic and idiosyncratic factors; (2) systemic factors are likely to be more important than idiosyncratics; and (3) the systemic nature of the problem requires systemic remedies, and these remedies are not available at the present time.

(i) the world financial system is plagued by a global liquidity problem; (ii) the IMF has no tools to cope with such a problem; and (iii) the only way to deal with it is through a reform of the international monetary system.
